title.es: Leer el guion de una escena

es: Leer un guion breve y distinguir diálogo, acotaciones y subtexto, explicando lo que un personaje quiere decir en realidad.

teaching.en: In a typical script, the dialogue shows what each character says aloud, while short notes in brackets describe what that character does.
teaching.es: En un guion típico, el diálogo muestra lo que cada personaje dice en voz alta, mientras que breves notas entre paréntesis describen lo que hace.
teaching.explanationEs: Script = guion; character = personaje; el diálogo se pronuncia y lo demás se lee.
segments: In a typical script, the dialogue shows what each character says
aloud, while short notes in brackets describe what that character does.
teaching.audioText: In a typical script, the dialogue shows what each character says aloud, while short notes in brackets describe what that character does.

teaching.en: A stage direction such as (She looks away and begins to whisper.) tells the actor how to move or speak, but the audience never hears it read aloud.
teaching.es: Una acotación como (Ella mira hacia otro lado y empieza a susurrar.) le dice al actor cómo moverse o hablar, pero el público nunca la oye leída.
teaching.explanationEs: Stage direction = acotación; whisper = susurrar. Va entre paréntesis y en presente.
segments: A stage direction such as (She looks away and begins to whisper.) tells the
actor how to move or speak, but the audience never hears it read aloud.
teaching.audioText: A stage direction such as (She looks away and begins to whisper.) tells the actor how to move or speak, but the audience never hears it read aloud.

teaching.en: The line «I am fine» is dialogue, because the character says it aloud in the scene, even though the audience may doubt that it is true.
teaching.es: La línea «Estoy bien» es diálogo, porque el personaje la dice en voz alta en la escena, aunque el público dude de que sea verdad.
teaching.explanationEs: Line = cada frase que dice un personaje; scene = escena.
segments: The line «I am fine» is dialogue, because the character says it aloud
in the scene, even though the audience may doubt that it is true.
teaching.audioText: The line «I am fine» is dialogue, because the character says it aloud in the scene, even though the audience may doubt that it is true.

teaching.en: The subtext is what a character tries to hide: she says she is fine, but what she really means is that she wants somebody to stay.
teaching.es: El subtexto es lo que un personaje intenta ocultar: dice que está bien, pero lo que realmente quiere decir es que quiere que alguien se quede.
teaching.explanationEs: Subtext = subtexto; hide = ocultar; mean = querer decir. Fórmula: says … but means …
segments: The subtext is what a character tries to hide: she says she is
fine, but what she really means is that she wants somebody to stay.
teaching.audioText: The subtext is what a character tries to hide: she says she is fine, but what she really means is that she wants somebody to stay.

teaching.en: A long pause before an answer can imply that the speaker is choosing words carefully, and attentive viewers learn to read between the lines.
teaching.es: Una pausa larga antes de una respuesta puede dar a entender que quien habla elige con cuidado sus palabras, y los espectadores atentos aprenden a leer entre líneas.
teaching.explanationEs: Pause = pausa; imply = insinuar; read between the lines = captar lo que no se dice.
segments: A long pause before an answer can imply that the speaker is
choosing words carefully, and attentive viewers learn to read between the lines.
teaching.audioText: A long pause before an answer can imply that the speaker is choosing words carefully, and attentive viewers learn to read between the lines.

teaching.en: In this scene the character asks about the weather because she wants to avoid the real topic, and the audience understands without being told.
teaching.es: En esta escena el personaje pregunta por el tiempo porque quiere evitar el tema real, y el público lo entiende sin que nadie se lo diga.
teaching.explanationEs: Evitar el tema real también es subtexto: lo importante no se dice.
segments: In this scene the character asks about the weather because she wants
to avoid the real topic, and the audience understands without being told.
teaching.audioText: In this scene the character asks about the weather because she wants to avoid the real topic, and the audience understands without being told.

prompt.es: Clasifica la línea del texto: ¿diálogo, acotación o subtexto?

choices.text: A stage direction: it describes what Sara does and how she speaks.
A line of dialogue: Sara says it aloud to the other character.
Subtext: it shows what Sara feels but does not say.

feedback.es: Va entre paréntesis y describe el gesto y el tono de Sara: es una acotación, nadie la pronuncia.

hint.es: Fíjate en el paréntesis y en los verbos que describen lo que hace.

origin.text: (Sara looks at the door and begins to whisper.)

prompt.es: Completa: «Ese significado oculto se llama subtexto.»

answer.text: subtext
accepted: subtext

feedback.es: El subtexto es el significado escondido debajo de las palabras, que el personaje no pronuncia.

hint.es: Es el significado que queda debajo de las palabras.

origin.text: In the script, Tom says 'Fine, go without me', but the long pause before it shows that he is hurt. That hidden meaning is called the ___.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Ella dice que está bien, pero quiere que él se quede.»

answer.text: She says she is fine but she means she wants him to stay

feedback.es: Says … but means … contrapone lo que se pronuncia con el subtexto: she wants him to stay.

hint.es: Empieza por She says y usa but para contrastar.

prompt.es: Relaciona cada línea del guion con su tipo.

pairs: (Tom sits down slowly.)
(She speaks in a whisper.)
«Fine. Do what you like.»
He is angry, but he hides it.

feedback.es: Lo que se hace y cómo se dice va entre paréntesis (acotación), lo que se pronuncia es diálogo y lo que se oculta es subtexto.

pairs: (Tom sits down slowly.)
(She speaks in a whisper.)
«Fine. Do what you like.»
He is angry, but he hides it.

prompt.es: Escucha la escena narrada y elige qué sugiere que la hija oculta algo.

choices.text: She asks her father to help her with the suitcase.
She avoids the question by changing the subject.
She says she is too excited to sleep before the trip.

feedback.es: La hija responde con el tiempo y el cansancio en lugar de hablar de la maleta: evita la pregunta, y eso es subtexto.

origin.audio: In the scene, a father asks his daughter whether she has packed for the trip. She answers that everything is fine, then asks what the weather will be like in the north, then says that she is tired. She never answers the question about her suitcase, and at the end she whispers that she will do it tomorrow. The audience begins to suspect that she does not want to go at all.

prompt.es: Explica el subtexto en una frase con «says … but means …».

answer.text: Tom says it is great, but he means it is bad.
accepted: Tom says it is great, but he means it is bad.
Tom says the food is great, but he means he dislikes it.
Tom says the food is great, but he means it is not good.

feedback.es: El gesto contradice la frase: Tom deja la comida en el plato, así que quiere decir que no le gusta.

origin.text: TOM: The food is great. (He leaves the food on his plate.)

prompt.es: Escucha la escena y elige qué hace Tom al final.

choices.text: He asks her to tell him about the project at once.
He goes to bed before she finishes eating.
He keeps her dinner warm without saying anything more.

feedback.es: Tom dice que lo entiende y guarda la cena en el horno: un gesto en lugar de más preguntas.

origin.audio: In the scene, Sara comes home late and finds Tom still awake at the kitchen table. He asks whether the meeting went well. She answers that it was fine and that she is not hungry. After a long pause she says that the manager mentioned a new project, and that she would rather not talk about it tonight. Tom says that he understands, but he quietly puts her dinner in the oven.

prompt.es: Escucha otra vez y elige qué sugiere la pausa larga de Sara.

choices.text: That the meeting was not as fine as she says.
That she is thinking about what to cook for dinner.
That she has not understood Tom's question.

feedback.es: La pausa contradice su «it was fine»: da a entender que algo del proyecto la preocupa.

origin.audio: In the scene, Sara comes home late and finds Tom still awake at the kitchen table. He asks whether the meeting went well. She answers that it was fine and that she is not hungry. After a long pause she says that the manager mentioned a new project, and that she would rather not talk about it tonight. Tom says that he understands, but he quietly puts her dinner in the oven.

prompt.es: Completa: «Quien se fija en los gestos sabe leer entre líneas.»

answer.text: lines
accepted: lines

feedback.es: Read between the lines es captar lo que los personajes sugieren sin decirlo.

origin.text: The script says '(He looks at his watch.)', but Tom answers: 'No, stay, it is a great party.' A reader who notices the difference learns to read between the ___.

prompt.es: Lee el fragmento. ¿Qué función cumple la acotación «after a pause»?

choices.text: It gives the actor a sentence to say aloud.
It hints that Sara is not being completely honest.
It tells the director where to place the camera.

feedback.es: La acotación describe una pausa antes de hablar: sugiere duda y contradice el «Really» de la primera línea.

origin.text:
SARA: (putting the keys on the table) It is a lovely apartment, Tom. Really.
TOM: You do not have to be polite.
SARA: (after a pause) I only said that the street is a little noisy.

prompt.es: Lee la escena. ¿Qué da a entender Sara con su última línea?

choices.text: That she is too busy to go to the party and says so openly.
That she is angry with Tom because he asked her twice.
That she does not really want to go, although she avoids saying so.

feedback.es: Sus respuestas evasivas y la acotación «does not look up» revelan que no quiere ir, aunque no lo diga.

origin.text:
TOM: Are you coming to the party on Friday?
SARA: I have a lot of work.
TOM: It is only one night.
SARA: Maybe. (She does not look up.)

prompt.es: Completa: «Una pausa larga puede dar a entender que se eligen bien las palabras.»

answer.text: imply
accepted: imply
suggest

feedback.es: Imply significa dar a entender algo sin decirlo de forma directa: la pausa insinúa cuidado al hablar.

origin.text: Even when a character says very little, silence carries meaning. A long pause can ___ that the speaker is choosing every word with great care.

prompt.es: Ordena: «La acotación describe lo que se ve, no lo que se dice.»

answer.text: A stage direction describes what we see not what people say

feedback.es: What we see y what people say contraponen la acotación (lo visible) al diálogo (lo que se pronuncia).

es: Usar adjetivos evaluativos precisos para describir trama, actuación y ritmo de una película y destacar lo que más gustó.

teaching.en: The plot is so gripping that, even though the film lasts almost three hours, nobody in the cinema looked at their phones.
teaching.es: La trama es tan absorbente que, aunque la película dura casi tres horas, nadie en el cine miró su teléfono.
teaching.explanationEs: Plot = trama; gripping = absorbente: no puedes dejar de mirar.
segments: The plot is so gripping that, even though the film lasts
almost three hours, nobody in the cinema looked at their phones.
teaching.audioText: The plot is so gripping that, even though the film lasts almost three hours, nobody in the cinema looked at their phones.

teaching.en: Although the ending is predictable, the central idea is so far-fetched that the director has to work hard to make us believe it.
teaching.es: Aunque el final es predecible, la idea central es tan inverosímil que el director tiene que esforzarse para que nos la creamos.
teaching.explanationEs: Predictable = predecible; far-fetched = inverosímil, difícil de creer.
segments: Although the ending is predictable, the central idea is so far-fetched that
the director has to work hard to make us believe it.
teaching.audioText: Although the ending is predictable, the central idea is so far-fetched that the director has to work hard to make us believe it.

teaching.en: Her performance was understated and completely convincing: she hardly raises her voice, yet we believe every word she says.
teaching.es: Su interpretación fue contenida y totalmente convincente: apenas levanta la voz, y aun así creemos cada palabra.
teaching.explanationEs: Performance = interpretación; understated = sin exageración; convincing = creíble.
segments: Her performance was understated and completely convincing: she hardly raises
her voice, yet we believe every word she says.
teaching.audioText: Her performance was understated and completely convincing: she hardly raises her voice, yet we believe every word she says.

teaching.en: Some actors seemed wooden, while others were over the top, and neither extreme helped the scene to feel real.
teaching.es: Algunos actores parecían acartonados y otros exagerados, y ningún extremo ayudó a que la escena resultara real.
teaching.explanationEs: Wooden = rígido, sin emoción; over the top = exagerado.
segments: Some actors seemed wooden, while others were over the top,
and neither extreme helped the scene to feel real.
teaching.audioText: Some actors seemed wooden, while others were over the top, and neither extreme helped the scene to feel real.

teaching.en: The pace is slow at first, but the final scene is deeply moving, which is why many critics forgive the long opening.
teaching.es: El ritmo es lento al principio, pero la escena final es profundamente conmovedora, por eso muchos críticos perdonan el largo comienzo.
teaching.explanationEs: Pace = ritmo; moving = conmovedor (no moved: moved describe a quien siente).
segments: The pace is slow at first, but the final scene is
deeply moving, which is why many critics forgive the long opening.
teaching.audioText: The pace is slow at first, but the final scene is deeply moving, which is why many critics forgive the long opening.

teaching.en: What annoyed me most was how formulaic the script felt: every twist was exactly what we expect from a thriller.
teaching.es: Lo que más me molestó fue lo convencional que resultaba el guion: cada giro era justo lo que esperamos de un thriller.
teaching.explanationEs: Formulaic = hecho con fórmula, sin originalidad; What … was … es la oración enfática.
segments: What annoyed me most was how formulaic the script felt:
every twist was exactly what we expect from a thriller.
teaching.audioText: What annoyed me most was how formulaic the script felt: every twist was exactly what we expect from a thriller.

prompt.es: Elige el adjetivo que resume el juicio del crítico.

choices.text: Gripping: the viewer cannot look away.
Predictable: nothing surprises the viewer.
Far-fetched: events are hard to believe.

feedback.es: Quien adivina cada giro desde el principio describe una película predictable, no absorbente ni inverosímil.

hint.es: Piensa en qué adjetivo describe lo que se adivina de antemano.

origin.text: Review: 'Every twist was exactly what I expected from the first ten minutes, so I was never surprised.'

prompt.es: Completa: «La actuación resultó acartonada porque recitaban sin sentimiento.»

answer.text: wooden
accepted: wooden

feedback.es: Wooden describe una actuación rígida y sin emoción, como la de quien recita un texto.

hint.es: Es el adjetivo que significa rígido y sin sentimiento.

origin.text: Nobody in the film spoke like a real person. The acting felt ___ because the actors said their lines without any feeling at all.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Lo que más me gustó fue la interpretación contenida.»

answer.text: What I liked most was the understated performance

feedback.es: What I liked most was + lo destacado forma la oración enfática: aquí, la interpretación contenida.

hint.es: Empieza por What I liked most.

prompt.es: Relaciona cada reseña breve con el adjetivo que resume el juicio.

pairs: I could not stop watching until the last minute.
Nobody would ever act like that in real life.
She said little, yet we understood everything.
The actors shouted every line and waved their arms.
I guessed the ending in the first ten minutes.

feedback.es: Cada juicio describe un aspecto distinto: la trama (gripping, far-fetched, predictable) o la interpretación (understated, over the top).

pairs: I could not stop watching until the last minute.
Nobody would ever act like that in real life.
She said little, yet we understood everything.
The actors shouted every line and waved their arms.
I guessed the ending in the first ten minutes.

prompt.es: Escucha la reseña y elige qué salvó la película para el crítico.

choices.text: The surprising twist at the end of the plot.
The fast pace of the action scenes.
The quiet performance of a supporting actor.

feedback.es: El crítico salva solo la interpretación contenida de un actor secundario; la trama y el protagonista le parecen exagerados.

origin.audio: This week I watched a thriller that everybody is praising, and I am afraid I cannot join the party. The plot is so far-fetched that I stopped believing it after twenty minutes, and the lead actor is so over the top that every scene feels like a school play. What saved the film for me was a supporting actor, whose understated performance was honestly the only convincing thing on the screen.

prompt.es: Escribe una oración enfática: «Lo que más me gustó fue el ritmo.»

answer.text: What I liked most was the pace of the film.
accepted: What I liked most was the pace of the film.
What I liked most was the pace.
What I liked most was the pace of the story.

feedback.es: La oración enfática con What destaca el ritmo: What I liked most was + lo que gustó.

origin.text: Lo que más me gustó fue el ritmo de la película.

prompt.es: Escucha la crítica y elige qué destaca el crítico de la película.

choices.text: The quiet performance of the lead actor.
How new the story is for the viewer.
The speed of the editing in every scene.

feedback.es: Destaca la interpretación contenida del protagonista; admite que la historia no es original y que el ritmo es lento.

origin.audio: I went to see the new drama expecting very little, and I was wrong. The pace is slow, yes, and the plot is hardly original, but the lead actor's performance is so understated that you move to the edge of your seat to catch every word. It is not the story that stays in the mind; it is the silence between the lines. I would not call it gripping, but it is undeniably convincing.

prompt.es: Escucha otra vez y elige cuál es la valoración global del crítico.

choices.text: Negative, because the slow pace spoils the film for him.
Positive, although he admits the film is slow and not original.
Enthusiastic, because the film is gripping from the first minute to the last.

feedback.es: Empieza esperando poco y acaba elogiando la interpretación, pero dice que no es absorbente: es positiva con reservas.

origin.audio: I went to see the new drama expecting very little, and I was wrong. The pace is slow, yes, and the plot is hardly original, but the lead actor's performance is so understated that you move to the edge of your seat to catch every word. It is not the story that stays in the mind; it is the silence between the lines. I would not call it gripping, but it is undeniably convincing.

prompt.es: Completa: «Aunque no hubo gritos, la interpretación fue contenida.»

answer.text: understated
accepted: understated

feedback.es: Understated es lo contrario de over the top: emociones fuertes contadas sin exagerar.

origin.text: The director trusted the audience, so even the saddest scenes felt ___ rather than over the top: nobody shouted, and nothing was explained twice.

prompt.es: Lee la crítica. ¿Qué actitud transmite hacia la película?

choices.text: Positive: it recommends the film without any reservations.
Negative: it advises readers to avoid the film entirely, whatever their taste.
Mixed: it praises the start and the lead, but criticises the ending.

feedback.es: Elogia la primera hora y a la actriz principal, pero critica el final inverosímil: la actitud es mixta.

origin.text: Review: 'The film has a gripping first hour, but the last act is so far-fetched that I wanted the thriller to end sooner. Even so, the lead actor is convincing enough to keep you watching until the very last scene.'

prompt.es: Lee la crítica. ¿Qué quiere decir el crítico con «formulaic»?

choices.text: That the twists follow a pattern so familiar that they no longer surprise.
That the twists are so difficult that most of the audience cannot follow them.
That the script copies a famous scene from another film.

feedback.es: Formulaic significa hecho con una fórmula conocida: por eso no hay suspense, aunque la fotografía sea buena.

origin.text: Review: 'Nothing in the script is surprising: the twists are so formulaic that the suspense disappears, yet the camera work is beautiful and the final scene is surprisingly moving.'

prompt.es: Completa: «Todos elogiaron a los actores, pero lo que mejor recuerdo es el silencio.»

answer.text: what
accepted: what

feedback.es: What I remember best is… es una oración enfática: what introduce lo que se destaca.

origin.text: Everybody praised the actors and the plot. Personally, ___ I remember best is the long silence in the last scene.

prompt.es: Ordena: «El ritmo era lento, pero el final fue profundamente conmovedor.»

answer.text: The pace was slow but the ending was deeply moving

feedback.es: Deeply moving intensifica al adjetivo moving; el contraste slow but … lo marca la conjunción but.

es: Comprender la actitud de los personajes en una escena de audio a partir de las palabras, las pausas y el tono, y describirla con sounds + adjetivo.

teaching.en: You can often recognise a speaker's attitude from the tone of voice alone, even when the words on the page look perfectly polite.
teaching.es: A menudo puedes reconocer la actitud de quien habla solo por el tono de voz, aunque las palabras escritas parezcan perfectamente educadas.
teaching.explanationEs: Attitude = actitud; tone = tono: lo que suena, no solo lo que se dice.
segments: You can often recognise a speaker's attitude from the tone of voice
alone, even when the words on the page look perfectly polite.
teaching.audioText: You can often recognise a speaker's attitude from the tone of voice alone, even when the words on the page look perfectly polite.

teaching.en: When she said great in a flat voice, it was a clue that she was being sarcastic rather than pleased about the news.
teaching.es: Cuando dijo «great» con voz apagada, era una pista de que estaba siendo sarcástica y no contenta con la noticia.
teaching.explanationEs: Clue = pista; sarcastic = sarcástico: dice lo contrario de lo que piensa.
segments: When she said great in a flat voice, it was a clue
that she was being sarcastic rather than pleased about the news.
teaching.audioText: When she said great in a flat voice, it was a clue that she was being sarcastic rather than pleased about the news.

teaching.en: As soon as I asked about the missing money he became defensive and began to snap at everyone in the room.
teaching.es: En cuanto pregunté por el dinero que faltaba se puso a la defensiva y empezó a contestar con brusquedad a todos los presentes.
teaching.explanationEs: Defensive = a la defensiva; snap at + persona = contestarle con brusquedad.
segments: As soon as I asked about the missing money he became
defensive and began to snap at everyone in the room.
teaching.audioText: As soon as I asked about the missing money he became defensive and began to snap at everyone in the room.

teaching.en: Her hesitant answers and her anxious questions gave the impression that she was afraid of making the wrong decision.
teaching.es: Sus respuestas dudosas y sus preguntas ansiosas daban la impresión de que tenía miedo de tomar la decisión equivocada.
teaching.explanationEs: Hesitant = vacilante, con dudas; anxious = ansioso, preocupado.
segments: Her hesitant answers and her anxious questions gave the impression
that she was afraid of making the wrong decision.
teaching.audioText: Her hesitant answers and her anxious questions gave the impression that she was afraid of making the wrong decision.

teaching.en: The minister was evasive and dismissive, so the reporters grew suspicious that the real reason was being hidden.
teaching.es: El ministro fue evasivo y desdeñoso, así que los periodistas empezaron a desconfiar de que se ocultara la verdadera razón.
teaching.explanationEs: Evasive = evita responder; dismissive = quita importancia; suspicious = desconfiado.
segments: The minister was evasive and dismissive, so the reporters
grew suspicious that the real reason was being hidden.
teaching.audioText: The minister was evasive and dismissive, so the reporters grew suspicious that the real reason was being hidden.

teaching.en: To reassure a nervous colleague, speak slowly, avoid sarcasm and give a clear clue about what will happen next.
teaching.es: Para tranquilizar a un colega nervioso, habla despacio, evita el sarcasmo y da una pista clara de lo que ocurrirá después.
teaching.explanationEs: Reassure = tranquilizar, dar seguridad a alguien.
segments: To reassure a nervous colleague, speak slowly, avoid sarcasm and
give a clear clue about what will happen next.
teaching.audioText: To reassure a nervous colleague, speak slowly, avoid sarcasm and give a clear clue about what will happen next.

prompt.es: Según la transcripción, ¿qué pista muestra que el hijo está a la defensiva?

choices.text: He uses a formal word to be polite to his mother.
He repeats his mother's question with great enthusiasm.
He answers with a question before giving any information.

feedback.es: Responde con otra pregunta antes de dar ningún dato: esa es la pista verbal de una actitud a la defensiva.

hint.es: Busca cómo empieza su respuesta: ¿da información o pregunta?

origin.text: Transcript: 'Mother: Where were you last night? Son: Why do you ask? Mother: I was only wondering. Son: Well... nowhere special.'

prompt.es: Completa: «Sonaba sarcástica, no contenta.»

answer.text: sarcastic
accepted: sarcastic

feedback.es: Sarcastic describe a quien dice lo contrario de lo que piensa; la voz apagada es la pista.

hint.es: Es el adjetivo de quien dice lo contrario de lo que siente.

origin.text: When the manager announced extra work for the weekend, she said 'great' in a flat voice. That was a clue that she sounded ___ rather than pleased.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Suena a la defensiva porque responde con otra pregunta.»

answer.text: He sounds defensive because he answers with another question

feedback.es: Sounds + adjetivo describe la actitud, y because introduce la pista: responde con otra pregunta.

hint.es: Empieza por He sounds y termina con la pista.

prompt.es: Relaciona cada actitud con la pista que la delata.

pairs: hesitant
sarcastic

pairs.es: dice lo contrario de lo que piensa

pairs: dismissive
evasive

pairs.es: cambia de tema para no responder

pairs: anxious

feedback.es: Cada actitud se reconoce por una pista distinta: pausas, palabras contrarias, respuestas secas, cambios de tema o preguntas repetidas.

pairs: hesitant
sarcastic

pairs.es: dice lo contrario de lo que piensa

pairs: dismissive

pairs.es: cambia de tema para no responder

pairs: anxious

prompt.es: Escucha la obra de radio y elige qué actitud muestra el alumno.

choices.text: Evasive: he gives excuses instead of a real answer.
Anxious: he asks the teacher to reassure him.
Dismissive: he says that the homework is not important.

feedback.es: Cambia de excusa tres veces sin dar una explicación real: su actitud es evasiva.

origin.audio: In the radio play, a teacher asks a student why his homework is missing. The student says that it is on his desk at home, then that his dog ate it, and finally that the teacher must have lost it. He never offers a real explanation, and the teacher's voice slowly becomes colder.

prompt.es: Describe la actitud: «Suena ansiosa porque repite la misma pregunta.»

answer.text: She sounds anxious because she repeats the same question.
accepted: She sounds anxious because she repeats the same question.
She sounds anxious because she keeps repeating the same question.
She sounds anxious because she asks the same question again.

feedback.es: Sounds + adjetivo (sin -ly) describe la actitud, y because da la pista que la demuestra.

origin.text: Suena ansiosa porque repite la misma pregunta.

prompt.es: Escucha la escena y elige qué quiere saber Ana.

choices.text: Whether her brother will accept the job in Madrid.

prompt.es: Escribe tu reseña de la escena: narra, destaca y valora.

answer.text: In the climax of the film, a teacher opens the door of her empty classroom on the night of the parents' meeting. She sees a chair, a letter on her desk and nothing else. She reads the letter slowly, drops her keys and says nothing for ten seconds. Then she switches off the light and leaves. What makes this moment so gripping is the silence: nobody speaks, but we understand everything. It is the small detail of the empty chair that conveys her sadness, because it shows that nobody came. The performance is understated, and the slow pace will pay off, since the tension keeps growing. Overall, I think it is the turning point of the film, because the audience learns the truth without a single line of dialogue.

In the final scene, a teacher walks into her empty classroom after the parents' meeting and stops at the door. A letter lies on her desk next to an empty chair. She opens the letter, reads it slowly and says nothing for ten seconds. Then she puts out the light and walks away. What stays in the mind is the silence, because nobody explains what has happened. It is the empty chair that suggests her sadness, and it is the pause that builds the tension. The acting is understated, and the scene is moving because it trusts the audience. Overall, it works as the turning point of the film, since the truth is learned without one word of dialogue.

prompt.es: Escribe tu intervención en el cineclub: recomienda, describe la escena y responde.

answer.text: I would recommend The Last Lighthouse to anyone who likes quiet stories, because it is worth watching twice. In the key scene, an old man climbs to the top of the lighthouse, sits down and says nothing for ten seconds. What makes the moment so moving is the silence: we understand his whole life without a single word. It is the small detail of his empty hands that conveys his sadness. The performances stand out, and I think the film will hold up when you rewatch it. Overall, it is well worth your time, and I hope that you will all give it a chance.

I recommend The Last Lighthouse to the whole club because it is worth seeing more than once, and I think that it will surprise you. Overall, I would strongly recommend it, and I would gladly talk about it again next week.
